target_customer: Engineering teams using AI coding agents who want shared sessions, plans and reviews (originally developers building AI agents who needed human approval steps)
problem: Agents need human sign-off to be trusted in production, and later coding agents lacked team collaboration. HumanLayer first sold an approval API, then a multiplayer coding agent IDE and cloud.
business_model: SaaS per seat (free Starter, Pro 100 USD per user per month, custom Enterprise) plus open-source SDK
product_category: Developer tools, AI agent infrastructure and coding agent collaboration

founders.name: Dexter Horthy
founders.background_notes: YC page says he started coding in high school at NASA JPL and spent 7 years at Replicated in engineering, solutions engineering, product and executive roles. No education listed.

founders.name: Kyle Mistele
founders.background_notes: Dealroom (Nov 4, 2026) calls him a co-founder who joined Factory with Dex Horthy; the AI Engineer speaker page says he co-founded HumanLayer with Dex Horthy and served as its CTO. The YC page lists only Dexter Horthy. He may have joined after the YC batch; join date not found.

technical_complexity.rationale: The original approval SDK across channels was modest engineering, while the later coding agent IDE and cloud with background agents is harder but built on third party models.

defensibility.rationale: The approval API and agent workflow layer were easy to copy by model vendors and agent frameworks. Founder thought leadership (12-Factor Agents) built mindshare rather than a hard moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Coding agent vendors absorbed collaboration features over time. The company itself was acquired by Factory, announced November 4, 2026.

market_need_then: In late 2024 teams were wiring LLM agents to real actions and needed approvals and audit steps; the launch drew attention on Hacker News in November 2024. No spend data found.

branding.domain_note: Used humanlayer.dev for the open-source and blog, now humanlayer.com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and opinionated, for example 'Do not outsource the thinking' and 'year of no more slop'

branding.brand_signature: 12-Factor Agents essay and repo, and the founder's coining of the term context engineering
branding.community_and_virality: The 12-Factor Agents repo is reported at roughly 23.5k GitHub stars by an aggregator; workshops and conference talks by the founder.

brand_strength.rationale: The name was a clear fit for a human in the loop product and the company earned outsized developer mindshare through content, but the name fit the original product more than the later IDE.

pivots.from: Human in the loop API for AI agents (approvals over Slack, email, SMS)
pivots.to: Multiplayer coding agent IDE and cloud
pivots.why: Not stated by the company in an opened source; a review site describes the shift. Date unknown.

outcome_analysis: HumanLayer launched in Fall 2024 as an approval API for AI agents, gained developer mindshare through the 12-Factor Agents work, and moved into a coding agent IDE. It was acquired by Factory, reported November 4, 2026, with undisclosed terms, plans to open source the product and refunds to recent paying customers. The exit looks like a team and product absorption, but terms are not public so the outcome quality is unknown.
notes: Directory status says Active, but sources report acquisition by Factory in November 2026 (not yet reflected in the directory). Round: the company homepage lists investors but no amount or stage; CB Insights (aggregator) shows a convertible note Oct 10, 2024 near 500K USD, treated as unverified. Caplight shows a Seed Nov 2024 with no amount. Kyle Mistele is recorded as co-founder and CTO from Dealroom (co-founder) and the AI Engineer speaker page (co-founded and served as CTO); the YC page lists only Dexter Horthy, and the Factory announcement itself was not opened. RuntimeWire does not give his title. Competitor search found no dated competitor list near the batch, so the list is empty. A different company called Dex (London recruiting) was excluded.
